title: Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis for opportunistic infections in children with HIV infection
objective: To assess the effects of routinely administered cotrimoxazole on death and illness episodes in children with HIV infection, and in infants of HIV‐infected mothers.
background: The majority of children with HIV infection live in low‐income countries without access to antiretroviral drugs. The prevention and early treatment of opportunistic infections are the mainstay of their medical management. Cotrimoxazole is cheap and effective against a wide range of organisms, including Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia (PCP), which is an important cause of death and illness in the first year of life. It is safe with relatively few side effects. Diagnosis of HIV in children is complicated by the presence of maternal antibodies in early life. Providing prophylaxis based initially on maternal status is one possible solution. However, routine prophylactic treatment is difficult to deliver in low‐resource settings, and could also lead to increased resistance to the drug.
selection_criteria: Randomised or quasi‐randomised trials comparing routinely administered cotrimoxazole versus placebo or no treatment in children (age less than 15 years) with HIV infection, or children less than 18 months with HIV infected mothers.

search_strategy.description: PICO-driven search for RCTs/quasi-RCTs of routine cotrimoxazole (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) prophylaxis in children with HIV infection or HIV-exposed infants. Concepts and synonyms: Intervention: cotrimoxazole OR co-trimoxazole OR trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole OR TMP-SMX OR TMP/SMX OR septra OR bactrim; Indication/intent: prophylax* OR prevent* OR prophylactic OR chemoprophylaxis; Condition: HIV OR human immunodeficiency virus OR AIDS; Population: child* OR infant* OR pediatric* OR paediatric* OR neonat* OR newborn* OR toddler* OR adolescen* OR youth* OR baby OR babies OR HIV-exposed OR perinatal OR vertical transmission; Outcomes context: opportunistic infections including Pneumocystis (PCP), serious bacterial infections, mortality; Design filter: random* OR trial OR randomised/randomized OR controlled OR quasi-random* OR cluster* OR placebo OR no prophylaxis. No date or language limits. Include studies from low-resource settings and pre-ART eras. Focus on routinely administered prophylaxis versus placebo/no prophylaxis in children <15 years with HIV or HIV-exposed infants <18 months.
search_strategy.boolean_query: (cotrimoxazole OR co-trimoxazole OR "co trimoxazole" OR "trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole" OR "trimethoprim sulphamethoxazole" OR "trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole" OR "sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim" OR "TMP-SMX" OR "TMP/SMX" OR "SMX-TMP" OR septra OR bactrim) AND (prophylax* OR prophylaxis OR prophylactic OR prevent* OR chemoprophylaxis OR "primary prophylaxis" OR "secondary prophylaxis") AND (HIV OR "human immunodeficiency virus" OR AIDS OR "HIV-1" OR "HIV infected") AND (child* OR infant* OR pediatric* OR paediatric* OR neonat* OR newborn* OR toddler* OR adolescen* OR youth* OR baby OR babies OR "HIV-exposed" OR "HIV exposed" OR perinatal OR "vertical transmission") AND (random* OR randomized OR randomised OR "random allocation" OR controlled OR trial OR "quasi-random*" OR "quasi random*" OR cluster* OR placebo OR "no prophylaxis" OR "no treatment")
